Hi, all. I have completed a formalization of an existence theorem for a counterexample related to the two-cardinal phenomenon in model theory, which plays an important role in the Baldwin–Lachlan proof of Morley's theorem:

For a complete theory TTT with infinite models in a countable language and an infinite cardinal κ\kappaκ, there exists a model of TTT where every definable set is either finite or of size κ\kappaκ.

I've published this result as a draft PR #42190. The PR is currently complete, compiling and integrated, while it is not yet intended for review of the whole diff. The main result is exists_model_of_card_definably_full in DefinablyFull.lean.

My plan is to improve the API on this branch, extract the reusable model-theoretic components into smaller upstream PRs, and then repeatedly rebase and shrink the draft PR as those components are merged. Eventually, the draft PR should contain only the theorem-specific construction and can then be marked ready for review.

At this stage, feedback on the overall architecture, module boundaries, and upstreaming plan would be particularly welcome. You may also refer to my improvement plan, which I sketched and had AI refine.
